text:
sara: Escalation from Acme — their CI started failing when installing redwood-sdk[ml] after we rotated the PyPI token. They see a 401 while resolving extras. Can someone triage?

sam: Ack, putting it on my plate. Do we know if they use poetry or pip in CI?

sara: They use GitHub Actions, poetry v1.5.1 with a private index in .pypirc pointing to pypi.redwood.internal. Works for base package but extras fail during build step.

sam: Can you paste the failing log from their run?

sara: Here — main failure (redacted):

```
  Installing build dependencies ... error
  ERROR: Could not install build dependencies for project
  Caused by HTTPError 401: Unauthorized for url: https://pypi.redwood.internal/simple/redwood-sdk/
  While trying to fetch wheel for redwood-sdk (for extras: ml)
```

michael: That looks like poetry trying to fetch the source distribution to build extras and hitting the token. Often happens if their token is set for simple index but not for the repo used during build isolation.

emma: Remote idea: after token rotation we updated token in our internal registry, but didn't add it to the read-only CI account secret we recommend for customers. Could be their secret not updated.

support-engineer: Customer says they updated the API key we asked them to rotate, and they tested pip install locally (on mac intel) and it worked — only CI fails. They also mentioned they call `poetry install --no-interaction --no-dev` which runs isolated build envs.

sam: Repro steps we should ask for: exact GH Actions job snippet, contents of ~/.pypirc used by action, `pyproject.toml` showing extras, and whether they pin build-backend (set build-system.requires). Also ask them to try `poetry config http-basic.pypi <user> <token>` in the runner env to see if it fixes.

sara: They responded with GH action snippet and pypirc. Key part: the action sets PYPIRC_TOKEN env var and writes a .pypirc file but uses it under the runner account user, while poetry build isolation runs in a temporary venv under a different user context.

michael: Known poetry quirk: PEP 517 isolation creates a venv and pip inside that venv reads pip.conf but not ~/.pypirc unless configured. For private indexes you need to set `POETRY_HTTP_BASIC_<REPO>_USERNAME` and `_PASSWORD` env vars or ensure Poetry passes auth to the build isolation.

support-engineer: Customer tried `poetry export -f requirements.txt` then `pip install -r` as workaround and that succeeded. So immediate workaround is to export and pip install. We should propose a longer-term fix.

emma: Action items: 1) docs: add a note about CI/build isolation + private index auth (poetry + extras). 2) Devex: provide GH Actions snippet that sets POETRY_HTTP_BASIC_<REPO> env vars. 3) Runtime: check if our internal repo accepts token scope used by their CI runner.

sam: Also ask whether their extras require building native wheels (torch, etc). If build isolation triggers source build, it will fetch sdist which requires auth too.

sara: I've drafted a reply with repro steps and suggested workaround (export+pip) and recommended GH Actions config. Sending it now to Acme. Marking as high priority until they confirm fixed. :thumbsup:

support-engineer: Thanks — logging this as incident-ref INC-2024-489 and cc'ing eng-ml for any follow-up on packaging to reduce build isolation installs.

dev-bot: New incident created: INC-2024-489 (priority: P2).

michael: Quick internal note — we should verify our private index honors token scope for `simple/` endpoints and consider returning 401 vs 403 messaging improvements so customers can more clearly see token vs permission problems.

sara: Good call. Closing loop once Acme confirms CI green.
